input.raw_level_dat_bytes_description: byte at offset 8 is NOT 0x0A (either the file is shorter than 9 bytes, or offset 8 lands on unrelated payload data) -- e.g. a bare little-endian NBT compound with no 8-byte header prepended at all

notes: Line 1291-1292's else branch: `nbtPayload = rawLevelDat` -- the whole buffer is handed to parseNBTRoot unchanged when the header signature doesn't match. This is a tolerant fallback, not a rejection: MSC 1 does not error here, it just assumes the header is already absent and tries to parse from byte 0. If that guess is wrong (header present but byte 8 coincidentally isn't 0x0A, or truly malformed data), parseNBTRoot's own `try?` swallows the resulting throw and metadata comes back empty -- covered by malformed-nbt-truncated-mid-tag-returns-nil and root-tag-not-compound-rejected rather than duplicated here.
